scope: Kaplan-Meier cohort survival, restricted mean survival time, segmented survival, Cox proportional hazards, hazard curves, cohort filters, population/exclusion accounting, event/censor support, privacy suppression, numerical stability, and aggregate-only governance.
confirmed_findings_fixed: Invalid minimum-sample configuration values were weakly coerced, accepted, or could raise low-level exceptions instead of failing closed.
Invalid durations and unknown outcomes were excluded without structured analysis-population and coverage accounting.
All-unknown outcome data could degrade to a generic insufficient-sample message instead of explicitly reporting unavailable event/censor classification.
Identifier-like or unapproved survival segmentation was not explicitly rejected at the engine boundary.
Segmented survival could expose cohorts with event or censor cells below the privacy support floor.
Cohort insights could expose exact attrition counts and rates when one outcome cell was below the privacy support floor.
Boolean/string/non-finite cohort duration filters could pass numeric validation or behave as numbers.
Cox covariate normalization could overflow on extreme-but-finite values.
Overall Kaplan-Meier estimates could remain available with unsupported event or censor cells.
Duplicate configured Cox covariates were not deduplicated and could break model construction.
Cox stability checks enforced event support but not censor support.
Cox results did not consistently expose the complete-case model population, excluded covariate rows, and coverage.
Kaplan-Meier tail at-risk counts below five could reveal small remaining cells and are now explicitly suppressed.
Internal aggregate summary fields are now suppression-aware and cannot reintroduce unsupported event counts or rates.
interpretation_boundary: Survival outputs are cohort-level estimates from employment origin. They are not individual next-period attrition probabilities, causal effects, or employment-action recommendations. Cox concordance is in-sample model-fit context rather than prospective predictive validation.
remaining_scientific_limits: PeopleOS cannot infer from the table alone that Tenure is truly time-to-exit for leavers and censoring time for retained employees; source-system semantics must be validated.
Kaplan-Meier validity depends on censoring assumptions that synthetic tests cannot establish for a real organization.
Cox proportional-hazards screening can flag assumption concerns but does not establish causal validity or absence of unmeasured confounding.
Prospective organization-specific validation remains required before stronger predictive claims.
